**Direct answer: No.** Both Stripe and AWS document time-bounded idempotency. A key protects a retry only while the provider still remembers it. After that, a retry can be treated as a new request, which could duplicate the operation.

**Stripe (API v1)**
- Stripe may remove keys automatically once they are at least 24 hours old. If a key is reused after it has been pruned, Stripe generates a new request. https://docs.stripe.com/api/idempotent_requests
- Keys can be up to 255 characters. Stripe compares incoming parameters with the original request's and errors if they differ. https://docs.stripe.com/api/idempotent_requests
- Stripe saves a result only after endpoint execution begins. Requests that fail validation, or that conflict with a concurrent request, are not saved and can be retried. https://docs.stripe.com/api/idempotent_requests

**AWS**
- The Builders Library describes returning a semantically equivalent response for the same request identifier only "for some interval". That is a bounded window, not a guarantee forever. https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/making-retries-safe-with-idempotent-APIs/
- The Builders Library says that reusing a request ID with different parameters returns a parameter-mismatch validation error. https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/making-retries-safe-with-idempotent-APIs/
- AWS Proton client tokens expire eight hours after the request. Retrying with an expired token creates a new resource, and so does retrying after the original resource was deleted. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/proton/latest/APIReference/Welcome.html

**Comparison:** Stripe documents a fixed 24-hour minimum for v1. AWS has no single limit: the window differs by service, and I verified only Proton's 8 hours from a primary page.

**Gaps and caveats**
- A search snippet said EC2 client tokens last at least 24 hours and ECS RunTask tokens have a 24-hour TTL. I did not confirm either on a primary page. The EC2 page I fetched only showed a retry-guidance table, so don't rely on those figures.
- The Stripe claims come from one publisher, and I found no independent corroboration.
- Stripe API v2 works differently: retries don't repeat successful operations, and Stripe retries failed or partial work to completion. I didn't find a stated v2 retention window in the text I read.
- I found no source claiming that idempotency keys make retries safe indefinitely.
- I did not export a report.

Sources:
- https://docs.stripe.com/api/idempotent_requests
- https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/making-retries-safe-with-idempotent-APIs/
- https://docs.aws.amazon.com/proton/latest/APIReference/Welcome.html
